name: client and browser
reason: Client factors with no artefact stating a procedure and an oracle. D08 has the right instruments, a real engine, a capture tool and a sanitiser bypass target, but instruments are not tests. Nothing here covers iframe sandboxing, service workers, extension privilege, webview bridges or Electron in any operational form.

L05-001.note: Origin handling is the subject of the CORS scanner, which is one consumer of the origin definition rather than a test of it.

L05-002.note: Site versus origin shows in which responses carry which protections across subdomains, which the header scan reveals per variant.

L05-004.note: The sanitiser entry is explicitly the bypass target. Parser state switching is the mechanism a DOMPurify bypass uses, and the entry states what a successful bypass looks like.

L05-005.note: Scoring a policy and naming the bypass for each weakness is a procedure with an oracle for whether inline execution survives.

L05-006.note: Policy bypass by injected code is the enforcement point question, observed directly.

L05-007.note: Context aware scanners imply a sink inventory. Neither states the sink list or tests one engine against another.

L05-008.note: A prototype pollution scanner states the payload and the sink confirmation, which is the factor as written.

L05-009.note: Gadget conversion is the impact step. The scanner reports the pollution, not the privileged behaviour it reaches.

L05-011.note: The capture reports postMessage shapes. Whether the receiver validates origin is not tested.

L05-013.note: Which capabilities a frame keeps, with the script plus same origin combination as the failure.

L05-014.note: Frame ancestors on every variant including errors is the coverage test.

L05-018.note: Credential handling is central to CORS testing, and the scanner focuses on reflection rather than ambient credential defaults.

L05-021.note: Classifying reflection with credentials is exactly the factor, and the scanner names the classes it reports.

L05-029.note: Storage key inventory and JSON body shapes answer whether a stored record contains a field the server considers secret.

L05-030.note: Captured URLs would show the state, and the entry does not test whether a secret persists in history or referrer.

L05-037.note: Content script scope against pages it did not intend.

L05-041.note: A native method callable from page script, with the injected object named.

L05-045.note: A file read from renderer script is node integration present.

L05-049.note: Electron fuse inspection is a REA operation that exists as a tool and has no entry stating procedure and oracle here.

L05-053.note: The import list of the loaded module is the authority, enumerated.

L05-061.note: Both are instruments against automation detection. Neither states which signal it defeats or how that is confirmed.

L05-003.note: nosniff on every response variant is the interpret-as-script question.

L05-031.note: Referrer policy per response shape is the same scan.

L05-016.note: Whether a child can navigate its opener is the matrix row.

L05-017.note: Isolation state and opener availability is the same test.

L05-023.note: Worker scope against intercepted requests is the factor.

L05-024.note: A cached authenticated response after logout is the oracle.

L05-027.note: What survives navigation is the same lifecycle question.

L05-028.note: Which stores are cleared is observed through the same capture.

L05-012.note: A message delivered to a frame that should not receive it is the wildcard target test.

L05-038.note: Web accessible resources fetched by a page is the factor.

L05-040.note: Permission breadth is read from the manifest and judged against purpose.

L05-032.note: A request triggered by a selector matching a secret is the oracle.

L05-033.note: Cascade impact on controls is the same injected style surface.

L05-034.note: Load events for fonts and images are the oracle channel.

L05-035.note: Performance timing is the other oracle channel in the same family.

L05-019.note: A cross origin write without a preflight is one of the messages the surface test sends.

L05-039.note: A message accepted across the boundary that should be rejected is the validation test.

L05-042.note: A local file or content provider URI readable from page script.

L05-043.note: Navigation to an external origin the host did not intend.

L05-046.note: A bridge method reachable with attacker chosen arguments is the preload validation question.

L05-048.note: The update channel state is read from the binary alongside the fuses rather than assumed from build config.

L05-050.note: Modified application code accepted at load is asar integrity off.

L05-055.note: Code executing despite the page policy is the interaction test.

L05-052.note: A native app rendered as web is the same bridge and navigation question.
